overview: The committee met to review annual surveillance reports required by city ordinance but was unable to complete the police report review due to the department's absence. The body discussed data storage and privacy concerns regarding parking enforcement technology before voting to table the matter for a follow-up meeting.

items.title: Police Department Surveillance Report Delay
items.summary: Chair Lazzaro reported that the Police Department submitted its mandatory annual surveillance report two months late and criticized the Chief of Police for failing to attend the meeting or respond to inquiries.

items.title: Parking Department Surveillance Report
items.summary: Parking Director Sarah McDermott presented her department's report, stating that License Plate Recognition (LPR) data is city-owned, stored in a secure cloud, and automatically blurs faces to protect privacy.

items.title: Public Comment on Surveillance and Data Privacy
items.summary: Members of the public expressed concern over the indefinite storage of surveillance data and potential information sharing between city departments and third-party vendors.

items.title: Committee Discussion and Motion to Table
items.summary: Approved a motion to keep the matter in committee and schedule a follow-up meeting to compel attendance and testimony from the Police Department regarding their surveillance activities.
